findings.passage: “Passing this constitutional amendment ensures Wisconsinites can trust that our elections will remain secure,” said Rep.Franklin.
findings.note: Press release after the Assembly passed the photo ID constitutional amendment (SJR 2).

findings.passage: “This amendment would not change state statute but would rather protect it from frivolous lawsuits and judicial activism. If you or someone you know is struggling to get a photo Id to vote please contact (844) 588-1069.”
findings.note: Same release; says the amendment keeps current law in place and points people who lack a photo ID to a help line.

findings.passage: This proposal would not make any changes to existing state law but would ensure future lawmakers and judges do not remove voter ID in the future.
findings.note: Franklin Flyer e-update titled Voter ID Approved By State Assembly; describes the photo ID amendment. Date from the official e-update list.

findings.passage: Photo ID is crucial to our society, in fact all 47 countries in Europe, along with Mexico and Canada, mandate Voter ID for most or all elections.
findings.note: Same e-update; argues photo ID is common elsewhere. Also says photo ID is required for renting items, buying medication or opening a bank account.

findings.passage: If you or someone you know is in need of a free ID please call (844) 588-1069 or visit here .
findings.note: Same e-update; points to free ID help.
